nodes.name: FeCoNiO_xH_y
aliases: Fe- and Co-doped hydrated nickel hydroxide

nodes.name: One-step solvothermal MOF synthesis
nodes.procedure: MOF-74 with 1D channel structure is assembled from 2,5-dihydropenthephalic acid (DOT; as ligand) and metal node, in which metal ions of Fe, Co, and Ni with different ionic radii can be uniformly integrated into homogeneous, single-phase structures and readily adjusted. Hexagonal nanorods of FeCoNi-MOF-74 supported on nickel foam (denoted as FeCoNi-MOF-74/NF) were synthesized via a one-step synthetic procedure (Scheme 1a, and Figure S1 and Table S1, Supporting Information), in which NF acted not only the support but also the source of Ni²⁺ for the formation of trimetallic FeCoNi-MOF-74.

nodes.name: Enhanced Kirkendall electrochemical oxidation
nodes.procedure: The FeCoNi-MOF-74 nanorods were treated with an in situ electrochemical oxidation process at a potential window of 1.0-1.6 V versus reversible hydrogen electrode (RHE) in 1 M KOH solution (Scheme 1a and Figure S3, Supporting Information).

At a current density of 10 mAcm^{-2}, Fe_{0.5}Co_{0.5}NiO_xH_y/NF... indicated by an overpotential of 216 mV and a Tafel slope of 32 mVdec^{-1}... at a much higher current density of 200 mAcm^{-2} the optimized FeCoNiO_xH_y/NF further shows an ultra-low overpotential of 257 mV... The durability... confirmed by the chronoamperometric test at a constant overpotential of 216 and 257 mV... current density can be well retained for up to 24 h (Figure 2d).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images show FeCoNiO_xH_y nanotubes with diameters of 70-300 nm and lengths of 0.3-1.1 μm with rough surfaces.
nodes.evidence_snippet: As shown in the images from scanning electron microscope (SEM) and transmission electron microscope (TEM) in Figure 1a,b ... After electrochemical oxidation, the size of each nanorod does not change notably (70 - 300 nm in diameter and 0.3 - 1.1 μm in length; Figure 1e), but its surface becomes rough.

nodes.characterization_summary: TEM reveals conversion of solid FeCoNi-MOF-74 nanorods to FeCoNiO_xH_y tubular nanostructures consisting of ultra-thin nanosheets.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Interestingly, TEM image, and EDX element maps and line scans reveal that the solid nanorod of FeCoNi-MOF-74 is converted into tubular nanostructures (nanotubes) consisting of ultra-thin nanosheets (Figure 1f).

nodes.characterization_summary: EDX element maps and line scans confirm homogeneous distribution of Fe, Co, and Ni throughout FeCoNiO_xH_y nanotubes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Fe, Co, and Ni still distribute homogeneously in each nanotube (Figure 1g,h).

nodes.characterization_summary: HRTEM shows ultra-thin nanosheets ≈1.5 nm thick with poor crystallinity, large amorphous regions embedded with ultrasmall crystalline grains (2-6 nm), and lattice planes of 0.215 nm (103) and 0.231 nm (200) corresponding to hydrated nickel hydroxide.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Moreover, high-resolution TEM (HRTEM) images of the ultra-thin nanosheets in a nanotube show that the nanosheets are ≈1.5 nm in thickness and feature a poor crystallinity nature (Figure 1i,j), indicated by the large amorphous region embedded with ultrasmall crystalline grains (2 - 6 nm) ... which shows two sets of plane spacing of 0.215 and 0.231 nm (Figure 1j) corresponding to the (103) and (200) plane of hydrated nickel hydroxide.

nodes.characterization_summary: SAED pattern presents weak concentric rings corresponding to (103) and (300) planes of hydrated nickel hydroxide.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The selected-area electron diffraction (SAED) pattern of our product also presents two sets of weak concentric rings that correspond to the (103) and (300) plane of hydrated nickel hydroxide, respectively (Figure S4, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: N₂ sorption shows large Brunauer-Emmett-Teller surface area of 111 m² g⁻¹ and hierarchical pores with sizes ranging from 1.2 to 9.0 nm.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Indeed, N₂ sorption measurements imply that FeCoNiO_xH_y has a large Brunauer-Emmett-Teller (BET) surface area of 111 m² g⁻¹ and hierarchical pores with sizes ranging from 1.2 to 9.0 nm (Figures S5-S8, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: PXRD pattern hardly shows any characteristic diffraction peaks, confirming poor crystallinity nature.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The poor crystallinity nature of our product is further confirmed by its PXRD pattern, which hardly shows any characteristic diffraction peaks.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-AES determines Fe:Co:Ni atomic ratio of 0.30:0.48:1 in FeCoNiO_xH_y nanotubes.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Fe:Co:Ni atomic ratio in nanotubes is determined to be 0.30:0.48:1 by ICP-AES (Table S2, Supporting Information).

nodes.characterization_summary: XPS confirms Fe exclusively as Fe³⁺ (Fe 2p₃/₂ 711.76 eV, 2p₁/₂ 725.26 eV), Ni as Ni²⁺ (Ni 2p₃/₂ 856.33 eV, 2p₁/₂ 874.03 eV), Co as mixed Co³⁺/Co²⁺ with Co³⁺/Co²⁺ ratio of 1.2, and M-OH hydroxide species (O 1s 531.42-532.59 eV).
nodes.evidence_snippet: The high-resolution XPS spectrum of O verifies the existence of hydroxides in FeCoNiO_xH_y as indicated by the peaks of M-OH (M = Fe, Co,Ni species centered at 531.42 - 532.59 eV (Figure S31, Supporting Information). ... the deconvoluted Fe 2p spectrum shows the peaks of Fe 2p₃/₂ centered at 711.76 eV and Fe 2p₁/₂ at 725.26 eV which indicates that Fe exists exclusively in the form of Fe³⁺ ... Ni also exists in only one valence state of Ni²⁺, as indicated by the Ni 2p₃/₂ peak at 856.33 eV and Ni 2p₁/₂ peak at 874.03 eV ... the addition of both Fe and Ni to Co further notably increases the Co³⁺/Co²⁺ ratio to 1.2 for FeCoNiO_xH_y.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS shows lowest charge transfer resistances R_ct1 = 0.08 Ω and R_ct2 = 3.48 Ω, indicating superior electrical conductivity and catalytic activity.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Among all the electrocatalysts, FeCoNiO_xH_y/NF (Fe_{0.5}Co_{0.5}NiO_xH_y/NF) shows the lowest R_ct1 (0.08 Ω) and R_ct2 (3.48 Ω), which thus indicates the superior electrical conductivity and catalytic activity.

nodes.characterization_summary: CV shows anodic peak charge of 22.7 mC corresponding to suppressed but significant M²⁺/M³⁺ redox activity due to Fe electronic interaction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The trimetallic FeCoNiO_xH_y also follows a similar trend as compared with its counterpart without Fe ... The anodic peak charge of FeCoNiO_xH_y with 22.7 mC.
